static_traits.name: Li Ming
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before; no psychotherapy received yet; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative; able to describe automatic thoughts specifically; tone carries frustration and Anxiety; tends toward self-criticism and doubting the effectiveness of new methods

basic_info.main_problem: I have a Catastrophizing pattern during outdoor activities. Whenever a small accident happens (such as falling off a bike), I immediately label myself 'terrible/unskilled', although such events are not common. This negative thinking affects my confidence in and enjoyment of hiking and cycling.
basic_info.core_demands: These negative thoughts are affecting my enjoyment of my hobbies and causing unnecessary stress and self-criticism, so I decided to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: Experienced a serious cycling accident several years ago, with high stress and fear at the time. Since then, whenever a minor mishap occurs during outdoor activities (such as a slight fall), strong negative automatic thoughts are triggered, gradually forming the cognitive pattern of 'one mistake means I am overall not good', with increasing focus on the negative parts while ignoring the overall positive experience.

core_beliefs: Making one mistake proves I am not good
My worth depends on achieving zero mistakes and perfect performance

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one accident or mistake occurs, it means my overall ability is insufficient and I should not continue these activities
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Engaging in self-criticism and developing thoughts of quitting (such as 'I should not be here'), reducing participation to avoid further mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am terrible; I should not be here

special_situations.event: Small mistakes or setbacks during hiking or cycling
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If zero errors cannot be achieved, it means being unskilled and unsafe
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessively focuses on negative details, ignoring smooth and pleasant moments; tries to suppress negative thoughts with positive self-talk and mindfulness (limited effect)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: One error shows I am not good

special_situations.event: When recalling a major cycling accident years ago or preparing for outdoor activities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If another accident happens, it will prove I am not suited for these activities, with terrible consequences
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Being highly tense during activities, anticipating the worst outcome in advance, seeking to 'protect' oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Something will go wrong again; I will mess up / get hurt

special_situations.event: After completing an overall smooth ride or hike
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as an accident has happened before, no positive performance counts
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Treating smooth experiences as accidental or meaningless, not recording or affirming them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These good experiences do not count, I am still not good

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as competent, keep self-worth, and enjoy outdoor activities again
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that mistakes will prove one's incompetence, leading to injury or negation again, thus losing self-worth and enjoyment
defense_goal: Reduces the possibility of failure and being hurt through self-criticism and avoidance
Maintains control and security with harsh standards

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent self prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Internalized as a dangerous and exacting outdoor environment/activity (which may 'judge' me with an accident at any moment)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes trying new methods or assigns homework
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying these methods will not work for oneself, believing failure is almost inevitable
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing doubt in a gentle but reserved tone: first acknowledging the advice's value, then emphasizing 'tried before with little effect', raising concerns, avoiding immediate commitment.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing details of major accidents or their aftermath
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equates the fear brought by the accident with current small mistakes, tending to replace emotional experience with rational description to maintain control
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using calm, descriptive language to state facts, minimizing emotional words, avoiding deep exploration of present feelings.

manifestations: Having several friends but not yet discussing one's negative thought patterns and distress with them
Produces a sense of self-isolation in activities due to self-labeling and self-criticism, finding it hard to gain resonance and support from others
outcomes: Persistently elevated subjective Increased stress and Anxiety
Intensified self-criticism, decreased enjoyment of activities

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Appearing 'I should not be here' and other 'should/must' phrasings
Views harsh standards such as 'zero mistakes' as personal rules that must be obeyed

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-criticism and labeling ('I am terrible')
Holding a skeptical attitude toward the effectiveness of new methods, trying cautiously, finding it hard to let positive experiences in

positive_force: Long-term participation in hiking and cycling, with some safety and technical experience
Willing to seek professional help and try assignments (recording positive experiences, using self-affirmations)
Able to identify factual evidence (most activities went smoothly) to refute negative beliefs
Has friend resources; potential social support exists
negative_force: Significant cognitive distortions of catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, mental filtering, and negating the positive
Traumatic memory of the major accident as a strong trigger cue
Lacking confidence in strategy effectiveness, tending toward doubt and Anticipation of failure
Not yet actively using Social support, tending to bear it alone

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing and self-labeling automatic thoughts during outdoor activities, accompanied by Anxiety and avoidance tendencies
antecedent: When preparing for or doing hiking and cycling
Minor mishaps occur (such as falling off a bike while cycling, small slips while hiking)
Recalling the major cycling accident from a few years ago
target_behavior.core_reason: The internal rule of 'mistakes equal failure' and attention bias formed after the major accident, with negative experiences dominating attention and Undoing positive experiences
target_behavior.function: Through self-criticism and avoidance, evades failure and potential danger, maintaining control and subjective security
target_behavior.consequence: Increased anxiety, decreased enjoyment, possibly reducing activity participation and persistent Self-denial
